formulations.label: Film-coated tablets
formulations.note: Tablets and the granules for oral suspension are not bioequivalent and are not interchangeable mg for mg.

src.q: Each tablet contains 250 mg cefuroxime (as cefuroxime axetil).
Cefuroxime axetil tablets and cefuroxime axetil granules for oral suspension are not bioequivalent and are not substitutable on a milligram-per-milligram basis

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Adults and children from 3 months: acute streptococcal tonsillitis and pharyngitis, acute bacterial sinusitis, acute otitis media, acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, cystitis, pyelonephritis, uncomplicated skin and soft tissue infections, early Lyme disease.

src.q: indicated for the treatment of the infections listed below in adults and children from the age of 3 months

Acute streptococcal tonsillitis and pharyngitis. Acute bacterial sinusitis. Acute otitis media. Acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis. Cystitis. Pyelonephritis. Uncomplicated skin and soft tissue infections. Treatment of early Lyme disease.

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand-specific prescribing restriction found in the cefuroxime axetil tablet SmPC; it advises considering official guidance on antibacterial use.

items.t: Acute tonsillitis/pharyngitis, acute bacterial sinusitis, cystitis, pyelonephritis, uncomplicated skin and soft tissue infections: 250 mg twice daily.

src.q: Acute tonsillitis and pharyngitis, acute bacterial sinusitis 250 mg twice daily
Cystitis 250 mg twice daily Pyelonephritis 250 mg twice daily Uncomplicated skin and soft tissue infections 250 mg twice daily

items.t: Acute otitis media and acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis: 500 mg twice daily.

src.q: Acute otitis media 500 mg twice daily Acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis 500 mg twice daily

items.t: Lyme disease: 500 mg twice daily for 14 days (range 10 to 21 days).

src.q: Lyme disease 500 mg twice daily for 14 days (range of 10 to 21 days)

items.t: Usual course 7 days (range 5 to 10 days).

src.q: The usual course of therapy is seven days (may range from five to ten days).

items.t: Children < 40 kg, acute tonsillitis/pharyngitis and acute bacterial sinusitis: 10 mg/kg twice daily (maximum 125 mg twice daily).

src.q: Acute tonsillitis and pharyngitis, acute bacterial sinusitis 10 mg/kg twice daily to a maximum of 125 mg twice daily

items.t: Children < 40 kg: otitis media (aged 2 years or older) or more severe infections, cystitis, uncomplicated skin and soft tissue infections: 15 mg/kg twice daily (maximum 250 mg twice daily). Pyelonephritis: same dose for 10 to 14 days. Lyme disease: same dose for 14 days (10 to 21 days).

src.q: Children aged two years or older with otitis media or, where appropriate, with more severe infections 15 mg/kg twice daily to a maximum of 250 mg twice daily
Pyelonephritis 15 mg/kg twice daily to a maximum of 250 mg twice daily for 10 to 14 days
Lyme disease 15 mg/kg twice daily to a maximum of 250 mg twice daily for 14 days (10 to 21 days)

items.t: No experience in children under 3 months. Tablets must not be crushed; the oral suspension may be used in children.

src.q: There is no experience of using Zinnat in children under the age of 3 months.
In children Zinnat oral suspension may be used.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to cefuroxime or any excipient; known hypersensitivity to cephalosporin antibiotics.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to cefuroxime or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1. Patients with known hypersensitivity to cephalosporin antibiotics.

items.t: History of severe hypersensitivity (e.g. anaphylactic reaction) to any other beta-lactam (penicillins, monobactams, carbapenems).

src.q: History of severe hypersensitivity (e.g. anaphylactic reaction) to any other type of betalactam antibacterial agent (penicillins, monobactams and carbapenems).

items.t: After SJS, TEN or DRESS with cefuroxime, it must never be restarted.

src.q: If the patient has developed a serious reaction such as SJS, TEN or DRESS with the use of cefuroxime, treatment with cefuroxime must not be restarted in this patient at any time.

items.t: Before starting, establish any history of severe hypersensitivity to cefuroxime, other cephalosporins or other beta-lactams. Use caution with a history of non-severe hypersensitivity to other beta-lactams. Special care after allergy to penicillins or other beta-lactams (cross-sensitivity).

src.q: Before beginning treatment, it should be established whether the patient has a history of severe hypersensitivity reactions to cefuroxime, to other cephalosporins or to any other type of beta-lactam agent.
Caution should be used if cefuroxime is given to patients with a history of non-severe hypersensitivity to other beta-lactam agents.
Special care is indicated in patients who have experienced an allergic reaction to penicillins or other beta-lactam antibiotics because there is a risk of cross-sensitivity.

items.t: Severe hypersensitivity (including progression to Kounis syndrome): stop immediately and start emergency measures.

src.q: In case of severe hypersensitivity reactions, treatment with cefuroxime must be discontinued immediately and adequate emergency measures must be initiated.

items.t: SCARs (SJS, TEN, DRESS): advise patients of signs, monitor closely, withdraw immediately if they appear.

src.q: If signs and symptoms suggestive of these reactions appear, cefuroxime should be withdrawn immediately and an alternative treatment considered.

items.t: Pseudomembranous colitis: consider in diarrhoea during or after treatment; consider stopping and specific C. difficile treatment. Do not give medicines that inhibit peristalsis. Candida and other overgrowth possible.

src.q: Discontinuation of therapy with cefuroxime and the administration of specific treatment for Clostridium difficile should be considered. Medicinal products that inhibit peristalsis should not be given

items.t: Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction may follow treatment of Lyme disease; common and usually self-limiting.

src.q: Patients should be reassured that this is a common and usually self-limiting consequence of antibiotic treatment of Lyme disease

items.t: Lab tests: positive Coombs test may interfere with cross-matching; use glucose oxidase or hexokinase methods for blood glucose (ferricyanide test may be falsely negative).

src.q: it is recommended that either the glucose oxidase or hexokinase methods are used to determine blood/plasma glucose levels in patients receiving cefuroxime axetil

items.t: Medicines that reduce gastric acidity (this tool applies this to PPIs and antacids): may lower cefuroxime axetil bioavailability and cancel the extra absorption seen after food.

src.q: Drugs which reduce gastric acidity may result in a lower bioavailability of cefuroxime axetil compared with that of the fasting state and tend to cancel the effect of enhanced absorption after food.

items.t: Oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin): increased INR may occur.

src.q: Concomitant use with oral anticoagulants may give rise to increased INR.

items.t: Combined oral contraceptives: possible reduced efficacy (lower oestrogen reabsorption).

src.q: Cefuroxime axetil may affect the gut flora, leading to lower oestrogen reabsorption and reduced efficacy of combined oral contraceptives.

items.t: Probenecid: concomitant use not recommended (raises cefuroxime levels).

src.q: Concomitant use of probenicid is not recommended.

items.t: CrCl ≥ 30 ml/min/1.73 m²: no adjustment (125 mg to 500 mg twice daily).

src.q: ≥30 ml/min/1.73 m2 1.4-2.4 no dose adjustment necessary (standard dose of 125 mg to 500 mg given twice daily)

items.t: CrCl 10 to 29 ml/min/1.73 m²: standard individual dose every 24 hours.

src.q: 10-29 ml/min/1.73 m2 4.6 standard individual dose given every 24 hours

items.t: CrCl < 10 ml/min/1.73 m²: standard individual dose every 48 hours. Haemodialysis: one extra standard dose at the end of each dialysis.

src.q: <10 ml/min/1.73 m2 16.8 standard individual dose given every 48 hours
a single additional standard individual dose should be given at the end of each dialysis

items.t: No data in hepatic impairment; hepatic dysfunction is not expected to affect cefuroxime pharmacokinetics (mainly renal elimination).

src.q: There are no data available for patients with hepatic impairment.
the presence of hepatic dysfunction is expected to have no effect on the pharmacokinetics of cefuroxime

items.t: SmPC: limited human data; animal studies show no harm. Prescribe only if the benefit outweighs the risk.

src.q: Zinnat should be prescribed to pregnant women only if the benefit outweighs the risk.

items.t: BUMPS (UKTIS, cephalosporins incl. cefuroxime): most studies have not shown harm; no extra monitoring for major birth defects needed.

src.q: Most studies of pregnant women taking a cephalosporin have not shown that it harms the baby.
No extra monitoring for major birth defects is required following use of a cephalosporin.

items.t: SmPC: small amounts in milk; infant diarrhoea and fungal infection possible (breastfeeding might need to stop), and sensitisation. Use only after benefit/risk assessment.

src.q: Breastfeeding might have to be discontinued due to these effects.
Cefuroxime should only be used during breastfeeding after benefit/risk assessment by the physician in charge.

items.t: No human fertility data; animal studies showed no effect on fertility.

src.q: There are no data on the effects of cefuroxime axetil on fertility in humans. Reproductive studies in animals have shown no effects on fertility.

items.t: Common: Candida overgrowth, eosinophilia, headache, dizziness, diarrhoea, nausea, abdominal pain, transient rise in liver enzymes.

src.q: The most common adverse reactions are Candida overgrowth, eosinophilia, headache, dizziness, gastrointestinal disturbances and transient rise in liver enzymes.

items.t: Anaphylaxis, Kounis syndrome, serum sickness: stop immediately and start emergency measures.

src.q: In case of severe hypersensitivity reactions, treatment with cefuroxime must be discontinued immediately and adequate emergency measures must be initiated.

items.t: SJS, TEN, DRESS, erythema multiforme, angioedema: withdraw; never restart after SJS/TEN/DRESS.

src.q: treatment with cefuroxime must not be restarted in this patient at any time

items.t: Pseudomembranous colitis, haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, jaundice and hepatitis.

src.q: jaundice (predominantly cholestatic), hepatitis
very rarely haemolytic anaemia

items.t: Before starting: establish any history of severe hypersensitivity to cefuroxime, other cephalosporins or other beta-lactams.

src.q: Before beginning treatment, it should be established whether the patient has a history of severe hypersensitivity reactions to cefuroxime, to other cephalosporins or to any other type of beta-lactam agent.

items.t: Monitor closely for skin reactions.

src.q: At the time of prescription patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.

items.t: Stop immediately for severe hypersensitivity or signs of SCARs.

src.q: If signs and symptoms suggestive of these reactions appear, cefuroxime should be withdrawn immediately

items.t: Take after food for best absorption. Do not crush tablets; not suitable for patients who cannot swallow tablets.

src.q: Zinnat tablets should be taken after food for optimum absorption.
Zinnat tablets should not be crushed and are therefore unsuitable for treatment of patients who cannot swallow tablets.

items.t: May cause dizziness: be cautious when driving or using machines.

src.q: as this medicine may cause dizziness, patients should be warned to be cautious when driving or operating machinery

items.t: Report rash, blistering or allergy symptoms straight away; report diarrhoea during or after the course.

src.q: At the time of prescription patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.
This diagnosis should be considered in patients with diarrhoea during or subsequent to the administration of cefuroxime

items.t: Combined oral contraceptives may be less effective.

src.q: reduced efficacy of combined oral contraceptives
